# Zoning & Development Analysis: 401 N Wabash Ave, Chicago, IL

**PIN:** 17101350382166 | **Address:** 401 N WABASH AVE, Near North Side (Community Area 8)

---

## (1) Zoning District Currently in Effect

This parcel is zoned **PD 835** — Planned Development No. 835, established under City ordinance number **13559**. This is the controlling zoning designation as recorded in the City of Chicago's official GIS system. [data:business]

**How to verify:** Confirm on the official Chicago Zoning Map: [https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning). You can also search the City Clerk's ordinance index for **Ordinance No. 13559** to obtain the full PD text.

---

## (2) Base Zoning vs. Something Else?

This parcel is **not** governed by an ordinary base zoning district (e.g., DC, DX, B, C, or R). It is governed by a **Planned Development (PD)**, which is a site-specific, negotiated zoning instrument. Under [1], Planned Developments in the Downtown "D" districts operate under their own approved bulk, use, and design controls established in the PD ordinance itself — the standard D-district tables are **superseded** by the PD's own standards for this parcel. [2] The regulatory overlay data confirms `in_planned_development: true` under Ordinance 13559.

PDs are reviewed and approved through the procedure described in [5], which subjects them to specific design standards (base/midsection/top articulation, upper-story setbacks, green design, etc.) in addition to whatever bulk controls are written into the PD ordinance.

---

## (3) Key Bulk & Density Standards

> ⚠️ **Critical caveat:** Because this parcel is governed by **PD 835** rather than a base zoning district, the authoritative bulk and density standards — FAR, height, setbacks, lot area per unit, parking — are contained in **the text of PD Ordinance 13559** itself, not in the standard zoning tables. I do not have the full text of PD 835 in the retrieved context, so I cannot state those numbers with certainty. The following reflects what the code says about PD-adjacent rules and physical data about the building:

**What the code says for standard D districts (which may or may not be modified by PD 835):**

- **Maximum building height:** [1] states there are **no maximum building height limits in "D" districts**. However, PD review and approval is required for buildings exceeding the thresholds in Sec. 17-4-0900. Note per [5], on **Wabash Avenue between the Chicago River and Ida B. Wells Drive**, upper-level setbacks are not permitted unless they occur above **55 feet in height** — this provision specifically names Wabash Avenue and is directly relevant to this address.
- **Setbacks (DC/DX/DS):** Per [1], side setbacks are not required. Rear setbacks apply only to floors containing dwelling units (minimum 30 feet), except that DC-12, DX-12, DC-16, and DX-16 districts are exempt.
- **FAR, lot area per dwelling unit:** These are controlled by the PD ordinance text — I cannot confirm the specific FAR without PD 835's provisions.

**Physical data on record for this property:**
- Building: **2,612,396 sq ft** of gross floor area (sourced from energy benchmarking records)
- Land: **98,019 sq ft** lot (approximately 2.25 acres, sourced from GIS)
- **92 stories**, built **2006** (this matches the Trump International Hotel & Tower)
- Implied FAR (actual, not necessarily maximum): approximately **26.6x** (2,612,396 ÷ 98,019) — for reference only; the PD-permitted FAR may differ.

**How to verify:** Obtain the full text of PD 835 / Ordinance 13559 from the Chicago City Clerk's Legislative Information Center at [https://chicityclerk.s3.amazonaws.com/legislative_documents/](https://chicago.legistar.com/Legislation.aspx) or request it directly from the Chicago Department of Planning and Development (DPD).

**ARO context:** The Near North Side community area has 20 ARO housing projects totaling 1,010 affordable units, reflecting significant ARO activity in this neighborhood. Any new residential entitlement at this parcel would be subject to ARO requirements.

**Brownfield note:** Several EPA-registered brownfield sites are recorded in the broader area (including Gateway Park Industrial Complex and Bloomingdale Park Trail sites). While none are at this specific address, environmental due diligence is advisable for any ground disturbance project.

**TOD significance:** Per [2], projects in transit-served locations within 2,640 feet of a CTA rail station entrance may be eligible for building height increases through a Type I Zoning Map Amendment or PD process. However, since this parcel is already within a PD, any modifications would require PD amendment.

---

## (5) Parking Requirements & Transit-Related Reductions

I **cannot determine** the specific parking requirement for this parcel from the available context. Parking standards for PD parcels are established within the PD ordinance text itself (Ordinance 13559), not the standard zoning tables.

**What is known:**
- The parcel is in a **CTA TOD area** and a **Metra TOD area**, which under Chicago's Connected Communities Ordinance generally allows reduced or eliminated parking minimums near transit.
- Per [2], transit-served location eligibility in B-3/C-3 districts (which may provide a reference framework) requires compliance with Sec. 17-3-0308 and approval via Type I amendment or PD procedure.
- The actual minimum parking for this PD would be found in Ordinance 13559.

**How to verify:** Obtain PD 835 text from DPD or the City Clerk; contact the Chicago Zoning Department at (312) 744-5777.

---

## (6) Maximum FAR and Building Height Allowed

| Standard | Answer |
|---|---|
| **Maximum FAR** | Specified in PD 835 / Ordinance 13559 — **not determinable from available context** |
| **Maximum building height** | No statutory maximum in D districts per [1]; the PD ordinance may set its own height; the existing building at 92 stories is already constructed |

The base Downtown zoning code sets **no maximum height** [1], and PD 835 would have established the approved height envelope for this specific development. The
